entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Vijay Kumar Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.

Heard Shri Vijay Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Anshuman Verma, learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the records.

2. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.609 of 2018 under Sections 376, 506 I.P.C. registered at Police Station- Kotwali Shahar, District- Hardoi.

3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 06.09.2018, in furtherance of an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. filed on 19.01.2018, stating that the informant is a widow, under allurement of marrying her, the applicant physically exploited her and when she got pregnant, the applicant declined to marry her and forcibly got her pregnancy aborted.
On 03.11.2018, the applicant came to her house and by keeping her child at the point of an illegal weapon, he raped her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Earlier, the applicant had filed Writ Petition No.34074 (M/B) of 2018 and his arrest was stayed by means of an interim order dated 28.11.2018 passed by a Division Bench of this Court.

After a charge-sheet was filed, the Writ Petition was dismissed on 04.03.2022.
5.

In the affidavit filed in support of the anticipatory bail application, it has been stated that the applicant is an innocent person having no criminal history and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
6.
In the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the informant stated that she is aged 30 years and she has two daughters.
The applicant had physically exploited her under allurement of marrying her but ultimately he declined to marry her.
7. In the additional statement, the informant stated that she had left her husband and had filed a suit for divorce.
In this statement, she did not say that her marriage had been dissolved or her husband had died.
However, in response to a specific question put by the Investigating Officer, she stated that her husband died two years ago due to fall from a terrace.
She stated that she was unable to give any particulars about her abortion.
8. The medico-legal examination report of the victim does not reveal anything significant.

9. In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she merely stated that her husband had died, she used to go to a District Hospital for getting medicine for her daughter where she met the applicant, who is from her village, and an intimacy developed between them due to which she got pregnant and the applicant forcibly got her pregnancy terminated.
Thereafter, the applicant forcibly made physical relations with her but did not marry her.
In this statement the victim did not state that the applicant had promised to marry her.

10. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.
11. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that the FIR does not disclose the date of death of the informant's husband or the time since when she was in a relationship with the applicant; that in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the informant has not stated that the applicant had promised to marry her and that the arrest of the applicant was earlier stayed by this court and that the applicant has no criminal history and the investigation stands concluded, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
12. Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application stands allowed.

13. In the event of arrest/appearance of applicant-Guddu Gupta before the learned Trial Court in the aforesaid case crime, she shall be released on anticipatory bail on their furnishing personal bond and two solvent sureties, each in the like amount, to the satisfaction of S.H.O./Court concerned on the following conditions and subject to any other conditions that may be fixed by the Trial Court:
